   1. General Information
       Introduction

    The Mansour Abad oilfield is located in Khuzestan province, approximately 10
     kilometers to the northeast of Behbahan city. This Field is situated in an area
     which is known as Dezful embayment and was discovered in 1356 by NIOC-
     Exploration Directorate. Asmari and Bangestan are the main reservoirs of this
      field which have been produced from 1386 and 1394 respectively. This
     structure is an elongated NW-SE trending anticline with approximately 600
     Meters of closure at the Asmari level. It is measured about 3km by 21km, and
       is situated at south of Khaviz structure and is on the same trend structurally
     with Lishtar closure of Gachsaran oilfield which is at southeast of Mansour
    Abad structure. Location map of Mansur Abad oilfield is shown in Figure 1-1.

                            Figure 1-1: Location Map of Mansour Abad Oilfield

      Pore and Fracture Press Prediction
     There is not any available data for Mansour Abad oilfield pore pressure and fracture
     pressure from NISOC.

      Program Outline

    The objective of drilling this location is to drill a vertical well to achieve more information
     about the structural ambiguities, also define the span of reservoir and produce oil from
     North flank of the Asmari reservoir in western section of Mansour Abad oil field. This
      well will be drilled vertically down to 2834m (-2450m) and completed as an Asmari
      Delineation/Oil producer according to the reservoir engineering specifications.

    The MB-W061N well drilling program has been written with respect to NISOC SOW
     (Attachment#10) and PEDCO geology program (W061N-MB-PEDCO-GP-0111-
     D03)

    MB-W061N well drilling sequences summarize as follow:

     26" Hole section:
    The 26” hole section will be drilled from 12m to 150m through alluvial deposit and
     Gachsaran Mbr. 5 formation with 63-68 pcf PHB & salt saturated polymer WBM. Then
     20” Casing will be set at ± 150m and it will be cemented in one stage with stinger up to
      surface. N/U 21-¼”, 2K CHH and then N/U 20-¾”, 3K BOPs (Annular preventer, Double
    Ram Preventer including Pipe Ram & SBR). RIH with D/Out BHA to TOC, perform 20”
     CIT. Displace mud in well by 75 pcf salt saturated polymer mud, D/Out shoe to 150m.

     17-½" Hole Section:
    The 17-½" hole section will be drilled from 150m to 1200m through Gachsaran Mbr. 5
     and Mbr. 4-2 formation with 75-95 pcf Salt Saturated Polymer WBM. Then CDR/GR Log
       will be run. The 13-3/8” Casing will be set at ± 1200m and it will be cemented in one
     stage as primary cementing up to surface. N/U 13-5/8”, 3K CHS and then N/U 13-5/8”,
    5K BOPs (Annular Preventer, Double Ram Preventer including Pipe Ram & SBR and
      Single Ram Preventer including Pipe Ram). RIH with D/Out BHA to TOC, perform 13-
      3/8” CIT. Displace mud in well by 105 pcf salt saturated polymer mud, D/Out shoe track
      to 1200m.

     12-¼" Hole Section:
    The 12-¼" hole section will be drilled from 1200m to 2354m through Gachsaran Mbr. 4-
     2 and Cap Rock formation (51m in CR) with 105-125 pcf Salt Saturated Polymer WBM.
     Then CDR/GR Log will be run. The 9-5/8” Casing will be set at ± 2354m and it will be
     cemented in one stage as primary cementing up to surface. N/U 11”, 3K THS and then
     N/U 13-5/8”, 5K BOPs (Annular Preventer, Double Ram Preventer including Pipe Ram
    & SBR and Single Ram Preventer including Pipe Ram). Cement quality log will be run
      to validate 9-5/8” casing cement quality after D/Out shoe track.

     8-½" Hole Section:
    The 8-½" hole section will be drilled from 2354m to well TD at 2834m through CR, and
     Asmari formation with 55.5 pcf Emulsion Mud and 56-63 pcf Oil Base Mud. Then Full
      Suite Logs and Image Log will be carried out over 8-½" open hole section to evaluate
     Asmari reservoir. The 7” Liner will be run and set at ± 2584m and it will be cemented in
     one stage as primary cementing up to ± 195m (10 Stands Wet) above Liner Lap. Clean
      out inside 7” liner to 5m above Liner shoe. Perform 7” Liner lap positive and negative
      tests and run 7” Liner CMT quality Log. C/Out 7” Liner and D/Out Magneset to well TD
   @ 2834m. Displace well with diesel as completion  fluid. Run 7”x4-1/2” Gas  lift
     Completion to ± 1950m. N/D BOP, N/U XMT. Perform well stimulation, clean up and
      well performance test operations. Secure the well and release the Rig.

   2. Geological Information
       Formation Description
    A brief description of the stratigraphic units expected to be drilled in Mansour Abad oil
       field typical vertical well has been presented in the following breakdown.

       Gachsaran Formation
        Deposition of the Gachsaran Formation is cyclic. This Formation totally consists of a
         repetition of Anhydrite, gray and red marl as well as salt and some limestone beds.

       Asmari Formation
       Asmari formation mainly composed of limestone and dolomite. This limestone is light
         gray, tan, Archie type I A interbedded with type I /II and II, Wackstone to Packstone
       by Dunham. The dolomite is sandy, Anhydritic and sometimes highly porous and
         fractured   crystalline  carbonate.  Microfossils   in  the  carbonates  included:
        Borelismelocurdica, Miogypsinoides, complantus, Elphidum sp. Rotalia viennoti, and
        Eulepidina sp.

   3. Nearby Wells
    As per geology program of this well and NISOC SOW, the well MB-W061N nearby wells
     are MB-011, MB-013 and MB-015.

      Nearby  Wells  Drilling  Challenges and  Lesson
      Learned
     Based on NBW study, the well MB-011 is a Bangestan Del./Pro. well and it’s drilling
     sequences are different from typical Asmari well for Mansour Abad development
      project, for this reason, all drilling challenges and lesson learned have been correlated
      to typical Asmari well sequences. Furthermore, there is not any available data for well
    MB-015 such as DDR from NISOC.

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned  in 26” Hole
         Section
      Generally, 26” hole section is first drilling sequence and it will be drill through Gachsaran
      formation in Mansour Abad oilfield. As per geology program, the 26” hole section will be
        drill through alluvium deposit and Gachsaran Mbr. 5 formation.
     This hole section main issue while drilling would be: Tight hole, Bit/stabilizer balling and
     hole deviation control.
    The best practice to drill this hole section is to commence drilling with low parameters
     and spud mud  for  first  drilled stand  in order  to prevent washout around  well
      location/cellar area, then increase drilling parameters to maximum gradually.
      In order to prevent Bit/Stabilizer balling, flow rate and mud properties must be in range.
     For  preventing  hole  deviation, use  stabilized BHA and  drilling  with  controlled
     parameters, if hole deviate from vertical, try to decrease hole inclination by reaming and
     changing drilling parameters.
      In this section it may necessary to displace spud mud with salt saturated mud in order
      to prevent tight hole and related problem in GS-5 formation.
     Furthermore, reamer trip is essential to make hole as smooth as possible prior to run
      casing.

     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
      1.  Tight hole and hard reaming while reamer trip in GS-5 with 65 pcf PHB mud (Well

                                                                                     Page 35 of 208

        MB-013).
      2.  Bit and string stabilizer balled up in well MB-013.
      3.  Tight hole while run 30” CSG (36” Hole size) in GS-5 formation (Well MB-011)
      4.  Hole deviation in GS-5 formation (Well MB-011) that corrected in next section by
        change BHA and drilling parameters.

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 17-1/2” Hole
         Section
    As per MB-W061N well geological structure this hole section will be drill mainly through
     Gachsaran Mbr. 4-2 formation.
     Based on NBW study and formation description, the main drilling issue in 17-1/2” hole
       will be tight hole, calcium ion contamination, hole deviation from vertical and CMT loss
      while CSG cementing.
     While drilling through Gachsaran formation especially Mbr. 4-2, drilling fluid must be salt
      saturated and Mw shall adjust with respect to hole condition, for example in case of any
      indication of abnormality while drilling/tripping such as Hi-Trq, upward drag, tight hole,
     increase in calcium ion value, etc, Mw should increase in 1 pcf increment to overcome
       drilling issue and prevent induced losses.
      In order to achieve good hole condition and reasonable ROP, flow rate must be as much
     as possible especially while drilling with PDC Bit to obtain planned HSI and keep mud
      properties in acceptable range.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
      1.  Tight hole in GS Mbr. 4-2 was main problem due to low Mw with respect to hole
          condition.
      2.  Calcium ion contamination in GS Mbr. 4-2.
      3. Observed high torque while drilling/reaming and frequent string washout in Well MB-
         011.
      4.  Casing stuck in GS Mbr. 4-2 w/ 91 pcf Mw due to bad hole condition (Well MB-011).
      5.  Noticeable CMT loss while CSG cementing in well MB-013 due to big difference
        between Mw (Mw: 90 pcf) and lead CMT slurry weight (Lead SW: 112 pcf).
      6. Due to lack of CMT return to surface (with no loss reporting while CMT job) while
        cementing 20” CSG (26” Hole size) in well MB-011, perform top-up CMT job with
        M.Pipe to fill annulus.

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 12-1/4” Hole
         Section
     This hole section is normally drill through Gachsaran formation then 9-5/8” Production
     Casing will be set in Cap Rock to isolate high pressure Gachsaran formation from
     Asmari reservoir.
    The key point while drilling this hole section is to adjust proper Mw with respect to hole
      condition in order to prevent hole problems such as tight hole, wellbore stability problem,
      string stuck and induced losses.
    As  per NBW  study, most  of  tight  hole and  wellbore  stability problems, mud
     contamination and string stuck has been recorded in this hole section.
    The best practice to drill safely through Gachsaran formation is to drill with salt saturated
     polymer mud and increase Mw in 1 pcf increment as soon as observed any abnormal
      sign while drilling/tripping such as Hi-Trq, upward drag, increase in calcium ion value,
      etc.

     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
      1.  Tight hole while connection and calcium ion contamination were main drilling issues
           in well MB-011 which cured by gradually increase Mw.
      2.  Calcium ion contamination in well MB-013.
      3.  Slight well flow in GS Mbr. 4-2 in well MB-013.
      4.  Complete losses as soon as enter in Asmari formation in well MB-013 w/ 126 pcf
        mud, cure same by cut Mw to 124 pcf and spot/pump several Mica LCM pill 20-25
       PPB.
      5. Observed string stuck in GS Mbr. 4-2 after complete losses in Asmari formation and
         high upward drag after free string in well MB-013 with 126 pcf mud.

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 8-1/2” Hole
         Section
     This hole section normally drill through Asmari formation that is porous, highly fracture
     and low pressure. Due to low reservoir pressure, the best available drilling fluid for
       drilling this section is Emulsion mud that must be changed to OBM in case of presence
      of shale in well path especially before Zone-4 of Asmari formation and Pabdeh
      formation.
    The difference between Mw (Even Emulsion Mud 55.5 pcf) and reservoir pore pressure
       is very high and it might induce formation losses and differential sticking.
      In case of heavy losses, try to cure losses by pumping acid soluble LCM, magneset

                                                                                     Page 37 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
         Mansour Abad Project
   N.I.S.O.C
                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project  Package   Issuer   Facility   Discipline    Doc.    Sequence    Rev.      Page 38 of 208053-073-9125
                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

     plug and use slick BHA and low drilling parameters especially flow rate in order to
     decrease ECD. Also, tripping speed must be as per surge/swab calculation to prevent
     induced losses.
      Also, in case of complete losses in Asmari formation or heavy losses,  it might be
      required to change drilling fluid system to Water in order to keep well column full and
     prevent subsequent problems.
    As per reservoir data from NISOC SOW, Asmari reservoir contains H2S gas, consider
    H2S requirements while drilling through Asmari formation.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
      1. Observed 2-4 BPH losses with 55.5 pcf Emulsion mud and 4-8 BPH losses with 60
         pcf OBM in Asmari formation in well MB-011. Furthermore, recorded max 40 BPH
         losses in zone-3 Asmari and 25 BPH losses in zone-4 Asmari that decreased after
        pumping LCM pill.
      2. Observed well flow 1 BPH and contaminated CMT in return 55.5 pcf Emulsion mud
           after drill 1m new formation below CSG shoe in Cap Rock of well Mb-011. Tried to
        squeeze CMT below shoe with RTTS w/o success. Change Emulsion mud to water
        and cont’ drilling to top of Asmariw/ NL-NG.
      3. Observed several string stuck while coring with 55.5 pcf Emulsion mud and while
         connection in Asmari formation of well MB-011.
      4. Observed 12 BPH well flow in zone-4 Asmari of well MB-011 with 60 pcf OBM.
         Furthermore, recorded oil and gas in return mud.
      5. Bad hole condition and several string stuck/hole pack off due to formation sensivity
          to water after displace 61 pcf OBM with water in order to control well flow in well
        MB-011. Change mud system to 64 pcf OBM but due to bad hole condition and poor
         progress decided to run CSG off Btm and cover troublesome zone in Asmari
         formation. Furthermore, losses start as soon as change system to water.
      6. Observed CSG plug while RIH and perform CSG cementing via RTTS after D/Out
        shoe in well MB-011. Observed heavy losses and no CMT return to surface due to
         big difference between Mw 64 pcf and lead CMT slurry 88 pcf.
      7.  Poor progress and low efficiency coring in well MB-011.
      8. Observed average 12-30 BPH losses while drilling through Asmari formation of well
       MB-013 with 55.5 pcf Emulsion mud.
      9. Observed noticeable losses while Magneset plug job and 7” Liner cementing job in
          well MB-013 but with good planning both job TOC was satisfying.
      10. Observed string stuck with 55.5 pcf Emulsion mud in Asmari of well MB-013.

        Sequence of Operation

    Drilling
      1. P/U & M/U required DP/HWDP stands for drilling this hole section, Rack back same
           in derrick.
      2. P/U & M/U Fishing Magnet, RIH to tag ground @ 12m and sure clean bottom, POOH
        and L/D Fishing Magnet.
      3. P/U & M/U 26” Tri-cone Milled Tooth Bit BHA as per BHA design, RIH and tag
        ground @ 12m.
      4.  Start drilling with spud mud and controlled drilling parameters to 32m to avoid
        washing out around Conductor Pipe and Cellar area and keep hole verticality. Pump
          Hi-vis pill to sweep hole as required.
           Drilling Parameters f/ 12m to 32m:
             -  WOB: 0-10 Klbs
             -  RPM: 70-100
             -  Flow Rate: 250-500 GPM
             -  Use high viscosity drilling fluid with minimum acceptable flow rate to eliminate
             the probability of formation wash out below sub-structure.
             -  Do not ream this interval.

      5. CBU, Run Totco survey, POOH & check Bit. P/U & M/U 26” String STB @ 20m, RIH
          to 32m.
      6.  Continue drilling f/ 32m to section TD @ 150m (The exact section TD will be based
        on 20” Casing Tally) with optimum drilling parameters, pump Hi-vis pill to sweep
         hole every drilled stand and as required. Run Totco survey to check inclination @
       100m and 150m.
           Drilling Parameters f/ 32m to 150m:
             -  WOB: 10-40 Klbs
             -  RPM: 140-160
             -  Flow Rate: 700-1100 GPM
             -  Use high viscosity drilling fluid with minimum acceptable flow rate to eliminate
             the probability of formation wash out below sub-structure and borehole.
             -     If reaming is required, ream hole to 32m with 60 RPM, 500 GPM.

    NOTE:
       Start drilling with Bentonite mud and low parameters to avoid washing out
           around Conductor pipe and cellar area and keep hole verticality.

                                                                                     Page 53 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
         Mansour Abad Project
   N.I.S.O.C
                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project  Package   Issuer   Facility   Discipline    Doc.    Sequence    Rev.      Page 54 of 208053-073-9125
                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

       In case of any deviation from vertical (based on TOTCO result @ 32m), adjust
                drilling parameters to drop the angle and return to vertical, such as decreasing
         WOB, controlling ROP, increasing FR, etc.
      Use LCM pill if encountered heavy losses. If loss couldn’t be cured by LCM pill
           use cement plug(s) to cure same.
       26” TD is based on 150m drilled depth. TD should be adjusted in such a way to
           have 1m of rat hole under casing shoe, the exact TD will be determined based
           on 20” casing tally.
       Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable
              condition.
       Ensure that adequate Fishing tools for this hole section are available.
       Ensure that enough Mud Material, LCM and Cement should be available before
            spudding the Rig to use in case of necessity.
       Ensure that enough water storage is available.
       Based on formation characteristic it might require to change mud system to salt
             saturated mud and increase Mw to max 75 pcf, make sure enough mud material
            are available.

      7.  At section TD, circulate and clean hole, POOH to surface.
      8. P/U & M/U 26” Reamer BHA, RIH to 20m, condition hole to bottom, CBU, Spot Hi-
          vis pill, POOH to surface, L/D 26” Reamer and Bit.
       Reaming Parameters f/ 20m to 150m:
             -  WOB: 5-15 Klbs
             -  RPM: 60-80
             -  Flow Rate: 700-1000 GPM

    NOTE:
        If observed any indication of drag while last POOH prior to run casing, run back
              to bottom, wash and ream to make sure that the hole condition is good prior to
            run casing.
        If required, increase Mw before run casing.
       Strap pipe while POOH. 

    Casing Running
      9.  Held PJSM. R/U 20” casing running gear.  
      10. Match the stab-in sub with Duplex float shoe on surface.
      11. Run ±150m, 20" casing with stab-in type shoe to bottom as per casing program.

                                                                                     Page 54 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
         Mansour Abad Project
   N.I.S.O.C
                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project  Package   Issuer   Facility   Discipline    Doc.    Sequence    Rev.      Page 55 of 208053-073-9125
                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

    NOTE:  
      Use thread lock compound to M/U shoe to shoe joint.
       Casing shoe should be adjusted in such a way to have 1m of rat hole and
           enough stick up (1.5m) on rig floor.
       Take care when running casing not to set down excessive weight if tight hole or
            ledges are encountered. Continuously monitor WOH during Casing running.
        Fill casing with Non-LCM fresh mud every joint to keep weight balance between
             inside Casing and annulus.  

    Cementing
      12. R/U False Rotary (or C-Plate), Run Stab-in sub (with new O-ring seal), 5′′ pup joint
          (with 5′′ x 20′′ bow spring centralizer) and 5′′ DP stands as stinger string in 20′′
         casing. Slowly lower stinger string and make sure stab into float shoe.
      13. R/U surface CMT lines and pressure test same w/ 3000 Psi. Break circulation slowly.
          Circulate 1.2 casing annulus volume with proper GPM.
      14. Held PJSM. Perform cementing 20” Casing as per program. Un-sting stinger, check
           float holding. Circ and flush stinger string, POOH & L/D stinger.

    NOTE:
      Any minor adjustment for CMT program regarding the corrected depth will be
           done in due time.
       Record and report the cementing pressure.
       Cementing Truck must equip with DAS to record job.
       After cement returns to cellar floor, open the 2" nipple on conductor pipe & flush
           same.

      15. Rest the 20″ casing on the elevator & WOC until cement surface samples get hard.
       Check for casing to be center inside conductor pipe. In case of any problem, report
         immediately.

    NOTE:
        If there is no cement return to surface, a Top-up job should be performed to fill
             the annulus, stage by stage until cement reaches the surface. Use the same
            weight as the primary cement slurry. Ensure adequate X-over for connecting line
            pipe to cement line is available. The cement should be accelerated with max.
        2% calcium chloride BWOC and no other additives. Wait for the Top-up job
           cement to get hard.

    Wellhead and BOP
      16. Check cement condition by slack off casing weight step by step, if ok, open window
        on CP and 20” Casing to drain fluids.
      17. Cut conductor pipe and 20” Casing, L/D same.
      18. Dress and bevel 20” casing neck suitable to install and weld CHH.
      19. Install and weld Casing Head Housing 21-¼”, 2000 psi on casing stub and test the
         sealing of welded casing as per wellhead specialist instruction (Limit test pressure
          to maximum 500 psi). Outlets must be aligned with cellar stairs.

    NOTE:
      The distance between CHH top flange and ground level must be 1.73m.
       Before installing the casing head housing, open all the test and plastic packing
             ports and clean inside with water and air.
      Check the 21-¼” wear bushing, 21-¼” plug tester and 13-3/8” Casing slip and
             seal assembly with CHH and Tie-down flange before N/U BOP’s.

      20. Install Tie-down Flange, 21-¼″, 2K x 20-¾”, 3K DSA and 20-¾”, 3K Spacer Spool.
      21. N/U 20-¾”, 3K BOP’s (20-¾”, 3K Annular preventer & 20-¾”, 3K Double Ram
         preventer including Pipe Ram and Shear Ram) and related lines. N/U bell nipple
        and flow line.
      22. Function test Accumulator unit. Function and Pressure test BOP’s as per NIOC
          policy.

     Drill Out
      23. M/U required 9-½” DCs, 8-½” DCs and 5” DP/HWDP stands to drill next hole section
        and R/B same in derrick.
      24. RIH with 17-½” Tri-Cone Milled Tooth Bit BHA including 17-½” String STB @ 20m
          to TOC.
      25. Circ and balance Mw. R/U CMT surface lines. Perform 20” Casing Integrity Test.
       R/D CMT surface lines.

    NOTE:
       Limit Casing Integrity Test pressure to 500 Psi.

      26. Displace mud in well with 75 pcf Salt Saturated Polymer Mud, Circ and homogenize
       mud properties.
      27. D/Out CMT, Shoe and Rat hole to 150m with controlled parameters.

        D/Out Parameters:
             -  Flow Rate: 500-700 GPM

             -  RPM: 70-90
             -  WOB: 5-10 Klbs
    NOTE:
       Watch carefully for any indication of abnormal torque, since there might be a
               possibility of shoe being backed off. In case, report problem immediately.

      28. Fill up the following forms and send to drilling office:

        Sequence of Operation

    Drilling
      1. Drilling 17-½” hole from 150m to 400m with Tri-Cone Bit. Run Totco to check
          inclination every 100m.

    NOTE:
       Perform BOP drill, H2S drill, Trip drill and Pit drill regularly.
       Perform BOP's test on each 14 days .
      Due to lack of data from NISOC and uncertainty regarding to Khaviz cap rock
              structure and fluid beneath cap rock, it is highly recommended to consider safety
            requirements while drilling through this hole section such as use Gas/H2S
            requirements (H2S Service, Gas Tight and H2S inhibitor additive for mud and
         CMT) must be consider before drilling this hole section.
      Choke manifold and choke line must be lined up for SOFT SHUT-IN.
      TD should be adjusted in such a way to have 1m of rat hole under casing shoe.
       Adjust Mw according to mud program and with respect to the hole condition. If
               tight hole encountered, then Mw should be increased a little more. In addition,
             the Lubricant and Torque-less should be added into mud system to reduce
                friction before running casing.
      The mud engineer should check the mud properties in a pre-planned and agreed
           upon time schedule for (Mw, FV, GS, FL, PH, Ca++, TH, Cl-)
      Use LCM pill if encountered heavy losses. If loss couldn’t be cured by LCM pill
           use cement plug(s) to cure same. Losses shall be cured prior to drilling ahead.
       Ensure that all drilling tools and equipment are on well site and are in serviceable
              condition.
       Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this hole section are available.
       Ensure that enough Cement and Mud Material specially Barite and LCM are
              available.
       Ensure that enough water storage is available on Rig site and water supply
            never cease.

      2. CBU, POOH to surface for change Bit. L/D 11” DCs.
      3. RIH with 17-½” PDC Bit BHA to bottom at 400m.
      4. Continue drilling f/ 400m to 900m. Run Totco survey to check inclination every 100m.

    NOTE:
       Perform Condition trip every drilled 300m (CBU, POH, RIH, CBU).
       Flow rate in above table are calculated based on maximum anticipated Mw.
          Keep maximum acceptable flow rate (950-1100 GPM) while drilling with PDC
                Bit.

      5. CBU, POOH to surface for change PDC Bit.
      6. RIH with New 17-1/2” PDC Bit and previous BHA to bottom at 900m.
      7. Resume drilling f/ 900m to section TD at 1200m.

    NOTE:
       Perform Condition trip every drilled 300m (CBU, POH, RIH, CBU).

      8. At section TD, circulate and clean hole, perform condition trip to last casing shoe prior
          to logging, RIH, CBU.
      9. Spot Hi-vis pill, POOH to surface.

    NOTE:
       Strap pipe while POOH.
      To either spot the pill or not prior to logging consult with Drilling Manager.
        If observed any indication of drag, run back to bottom, wash and ream to make
            sure that the hole condition is good prior to run log.
      Do not forget to change Top Ram before/after running logs.

    Logging
      10. Change Ram, install shooting Nipple, test upper Ram, R/U wireline Eq., Run
      CDR/GR log. R/D Wireline Eq., Change Ram.
      11. RIH w/ last BHA to bottom in order to condition hole prior to CSG running, CBU,
        Spot Hi-vis pill, POOH.

    NOTE:
      To either spot the pill or not prior to CSG running consult with Drilling Manager.
        If observed any indication of drag, run back to bottom, wash and ream to make
            sure that the hole condition is good for casing running.
        If required, increase Mw before run Casing.

    Casing Running
      12. Held PJSM. R/Up 13-3/8” casing running gear.  
      13. Run 13-3/8″ casing to bottom at 1200m as per casing program. Casing shoe should
        be adjusted in such a way to have 1m of rat hole and enough stick up (1.5m) on rig
           floor and fill casing by Non-LCM fresh mud each 5 joints.  

    NOTE:

                       Project  Package   Issuer   Facility   Discipline    Doc.    Sequence    Rev.      Page 61 of 208053-073-9125
                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

      Use thread lock compound to M/U all shoe track connections.
       Casing shoe should be adjusted in such a way to have 1m of rat hole and
           enough stick up (1.5m) on rig floor.
       Take care when running casing not to set down excessive weight if tight hole or
            ledges are encountered. Continuously monitor WOH during Casing running.
        Fill casing with Non-LCM fresh mud every 5 joints.

    Cementing
      14. R/U cement head and CMT surface lines. Test the lines to 3000 psi for 15 minutes.
      15. Cement casing as per program. Displace CMT with mud and Bump the plugs with
        1500 psi. Bleed off pressure and check for back flow.

    NOTE:
      Any minor adjustment for Cementing program regarding the corrected depth will
           be done in due time.
       Record and report the final pressure before bump the plug.
       Cementing Truck must equipped with DAS to record job.
        If cement returns to surface and observe bumping w/ 1500 psi while displacing
           cement slurry, hold pressure for 15 minutes and assume bumping pressure as
           Casing integrity test and note in DDR.
        If bumping was not observed, casing integrity test must be performed before
                drilling out collar and shoe track (at least 24 hours after cementing).
        If any back flow observed after Bleed off pressure, hold the pressure inside for
             the cement to get hard.
        If there is no cement return to surface, a top-up job should be performed to fill
             the annulus, stage by stage until cement reaches the surface.

    Wellhead and BOP
      16. Flush BOPs. Hold on Casing string weight.
      17. Hang BOPs. Set 21-¼” x 13-3/8” casing slip in place, slack off casing weight, test
      CSG Slip as per WH engineer instruction (Open base flange side outlet valves while
           testing).
      18. Rough cut 13-3/8” landing joint, L/D same. N/D 20-¾”, 3K BOP’s. Dress and bevel
         13-3/8” casing neck.  
      19. Install Casing Head Spool 21-¼”, 2K x 13-5/8”, 3K. Pack and test CHS P-seals as
         per WH engineer instruction (Limit pressure to a maximum 1000 Psi)

    NOTE:

                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

       Before installing the casing head spool, open all the test and plastic packing
             ports and clean inside it with water and air.
      Do not forget to check the 13-5/8” wear bushing, 13-5/8” plug tester and 9-5/8”
           Casing slip and seal assembly with CHS and tie down flange before installing
          CHS.

      20. Install Tie down Flange, 13-5/8”, 3K x 13-5/8”, 5K DSA and 13-5/8”, 5K Spacer
         Spool.
      21. N/U 13-5/8”, 5K BOPs (13-5/8”, 5K Annular preventer, 13-5/8″, 5K Double Ram
         preventer including Pipe Ram and Shear/Blind Ram & 13-5/8”, 5K Single Pipe Ram
         preventer) and related lines. N/U bell nipple and flow line.
      22. Function test Accumulator unit, Function & Pressure Test BOPs and related lines
        as per NIOC standard.

    D/Out
      23. L/D 9-1/2″ DCs, P/U & M/U required 8-1/2″ DCs and 5″ DP/HWDP stands for drill
         next hole section.
      24. P/U & M/U 12-1/4″ Tri-cone Milled Tooth Bit BHA including Junk sub, RIH to tag
         plugs.
      25. Circ and balance Mw. R/U CMT surface lines. Perform 13-3/8” Casing Integrity Test,
       R/D CMT surface lines.

    NOTE:
       Limit Casing Integrity Test pressure to max 1000 Psi.

        Sequence of Operation

    Drilling
      1. Drilling 12-¼″ hole from 1200m to 1220m, work on junk sub, CBU, POOH.
      2. P/U & M/U 12-¼″ PDC Bit BHA (Including 12-¼″ St. STB @ 20m), RIH to bottom @
        1220m.
      3. Resume drilling f/ 1220m to 1800m.

    NOTE:
       Perform BOP drill, Trip drill and Pit drill regularly.
       Perform BOP's test on each 14 days.
      Choke manifold and choke line must be lined up for SOFT SHUT-IN.
      TD will be based on 51m drilled in CR below KB/E. The final TD will be based
           on formation tops detected by the well site geologist.
      TD should be adjusted in such a way to drill the rat hole as minimum as possible.
       Adjust Mw according to mud program and with respect to the hole condition. If
               tight hole encountered, then the Mw should be increased a  little more. In
              addition, the Lubricant and Torque-less should be added into mud system to
           reduce friction before running casing.
      The mud engineer should check the mud properties in a pre-planned and agreed
           upon time schedule for (Mw, FV, GS, FL, PH, Ca++, TH, Cl-)
       Ensure that enough amount and type of LCM are available at Rig site and keep
            ready to mix and pump LCM Pills to cure losses.
       Ensure that adequate fishing tools for this section are available.
       Ensure that enough water storage is available on Rig site and water supply
            never cease.
       Perform Condition trip every drilled 300m (CBU, POH, RIH, CBU).
       Flow rate in above table are calculated based on maximum anticipated Mw.
          Keep maximum acceptable flow rate (600-800 GPM) while drilling with PDC Bit.

      4. CBU, POOH to surface to change Bit.
      5. P/U & M/U New 12-¼″ PDC Bit and last BHA, RIH to bottom @ 1800m.
      6. Resume drilling f/ 1800m to section TD @ 2354m (51m inside Cap Rock Below KB/E).
      7. At section TD, Circulate and clean hole. Perform condition trip to last casing shoe
           prior to logging, rest hole for 1 hr., RIH to bottom and check the hole for any fill at
         bottom, CBU, check Btm’s up sample for any influx, Spot pill, POOH.

    NOTE:
       Strap pipe while POOH.
      To either spot the pill or not prior to logging consult with Drilling Manager.

       Mud Discussion
     This section will be drilled ±150m through Alluvial and Gachsaran Formation and  it
      contains of Anhydrite, gray and red marl as well as salt and some limestone beds.
     This hole section will be drilled by using Bentonite mud and Mud can be lubricated with
     1-2 % by volume of lubricant.
    PHB pill will be used to clean the hole and since Bentonite has the best cake around
      the well bore, it will make a good cake for hole stability.

                Mixing Procedure
    Mud Type: Bentonite Mud

      1.   Fill the pit with drill water 0.98 bbl/ bbl.
      2. Add 1-3 lb/bbl of Soda Ash to treat out any hardness.
      3. Add 0.5-1 lb/bbl of Caustic Soda to raise the pH above 10.
      4. Add 25‐35 lb/bbl Bentonite, use maximum searing capacity to pre‐hydrate
         Bentonite.

         Engineering Comments

            Mud Weight
       Drilling fluid density will be controlled around 63-68 pcf. Use available solids control
     equipment to reduce low gravity solids build-up, thus reducing any dilution requirements
       for density control. Mud weight to be adjusted as hole conditions dictate.

               Funnel Viscosity
     Funnel  viscosity more than 70  (sec/qrt)  is enough.  Plastic  viscosity should be

     API Fluid loss will not be controlled while drilling this section.

     During normal drilling operations, PH should be kept 10-11 this will maximize chemicals

            MBT
     Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT doesn’t need
      to be controlled in this hole section when Spud mud designed as this section DF system.

                 Solid Control Equipment
       All SCE should be function tested and repaired as necessary prior to spud the well.
     Dress Shakers with 60 - 80 mesh size screen and mud cleaner with 140 – 175.
     Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.
    Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear
     motion shale shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all
      the time at high flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids and

           Drilling Issue

               Stuck Pipe
     Evidences of tight hole and stuck pipe occurred in the offset wells while drilling the shale
      formation. Mud must be inhibited to avoid the reaction with the shale. In case of stuck
      pipe, PIPE pill at 3‐4 gal/bbl of Diesel can be spotted around the stuck area.

               Hole Cleaning
    The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 readings. The 6
     reading has to be over 10 all time to ensure good hole cleaning.

                  Lubricity
      In case of high torque & drag, LUBRICANT or diesel would be used at 1 ‐ 2% by volume.

                  Circulation
     There may be a requirement to dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of
      circulations in order to minimize loss of mud and to allow full dispersion of hydrate-able
     polymers.

            Down Hole Losses
     Losses are expected while drilling this section. The concentration of LCM will vary
     according to losses. In the event of seepage losses, treat system with a finer grade of
    LCM at 10 – 15 lb/bbl. In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare
       pills at different graded concentrations and spot over thief zone. The concentration may
     vary between 20 – 70 lb/bbl.
     Ensure that the driller displace the LCM pill out of the string prior to shutting down the
    mud pumps. In the event of severe losses, cross linking pills should be pumped to
     minimize losses.

         Personal Safety

                 Introduction
     Although water Base Muds do not have the inherent safety risk which are associated
      with Oil Based Muds, care must be used at all times while handling these muds to avoid
     any potential risk or hazard associated with drilling fluids.

                Basic Risks to Health and Safety
       All drilling fluids are potentially harmful and excessive skin contact must be avoided.
     There are wide ranges of products associated with the various water-based mud system
     and it is therefore essential that the relevant MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet) is read
     and that you are aware of the potential hazards involved prior to using these products.
      Brines, caustic, lime and water based with high pH can all cause chemical burns  if
     allowed prolonged contact with the skin. It is essential that contact with eyes is avoided.
     Handle wearing goggles, gloves and overalls.
     Corrosion inhibitors and biocides are extremely harmful. These products must be
     handled with care and proper safety precautions i.e. use of gloves, goggles etc. must
     be taken. Spillage of polymers must be covered with sand and cleaned up using a
      shovel.
    The contaminated area should then be thoroughly washed.
     Adding water immediately makes it harder to clean up the spill and also makes the floor
     extremely slippery.

                                                                                     Page 93 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
         Mansour Abad Project
   N.I.S.O.C

Contract No:
                       Project  Package   Issuer   Facility   Discipline    Doc.    Sequence    Rev.      Page 94 of 208053-073-9125
                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

         If overalls become severely contaminated, they should be changed as soon as possible
     and must be properly cleaned before re‐use.
      Barrier creams are available to prevent contact of mud etc. with the hands or arms.
     These creams are generally for oil-based mud but they do offer protection from water-
     based mud although their efficiency is reduced.
       All safety regulations must be strictly observed. Know where eye wash facilities and
     emergency stations are located prior to commencing work. The mud kit may include
     Barium Chloride which is a Class I poison and great care must be taken should its use
    become necessary. Pipettes must not be used with Barium Chloride. The reagents 5N
      Sulphuric acid and 8N potassium hydroxide are strong acid and alkali respectively, and
     care and safety precautions e.g. safety glasses etc., must be taken during their use.

                 Information of Components
    As with Oil Based Muds, sacked material can present a number of hazards. Material
     Safety Data Sheets contain health and safety data and safe‐handling procedures.
    MSDS sheets must be readily available at a work site any time hazardous products are
      present, whether workers are present or not.
    MSDS for products are available in Farsi & English on computer disks, hard copies and
      big posters. Training workers to understand the contents of MSDS sheets is mandatory
      to prepare them to read and under‐stand hazard warning labels.
      Training also must include sections devoted to health studies, routes of exposure the
      appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

       Mud Discussion

    The 17-1/2” section will be drilled from 20" Casing Shoe @ ±150m to ±1200m with 75pcf
      Salt Saturated mud and gradually become to (75-95pcf) Salt saturated Polymer Mud to
     an estimated section TD (1200 m). During drilling second interval of this section the well
       will be sweep by Hi-Vis KCl/PHPA Pill.
     At this system uses Salt as the source of density and Clay inhibition in the system. Mud
     weight will be Increase to 95 pcf by Barite as weighting agent; Rheology will be
      controlled by the use of XC polymer. Also, Fluid loss will be kept under control by the
      addition of polymeric chemicals such as, Starch Addition of Drilling Detergent (As
     contingency) and KCl pill can prevent bit balling and consequently can help to optimize
      the drilling operation while drilling sticky Marl and Clay section. Fluid loss should be kept
     around 5 cc/30min, meanwhile.
      Also, PH should be maintained within 9 - 9.5 while drilling Marl and keep within 9.5 – 10
      while drilling Anhydrite.
     At this section for the inhibition of system must be use PHPA (0.2 – 0.3 ppb) which
     adheres to the surface of the drilled cuttings, encapsulating them, and also coating the
      well bore reducing the hydration of clays in the formation.
      After drilling shoe track and rat hole with carried Bentonite mud from previous section
     Salt/Polymer mud will be employed to drilling this hole section.
     Saturated Salt Muds are primarily used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while
       drilling massive salt beds. They can also be used to reduce dispersion and hydration of
     shales and clays.
     Potassium chloride is the primary source of the potassium ions in this system. In case
      of soft, sticky red Marl & Clay which encountered problems such as bit balling additions
      of drilling KCl (3-5 %) to inhibit clays in Gachsaran is recommended.
     Potassium is used in areas where inhibition is required to limit chemical alteration of
      shales. Potassium performance is based on cationic exchange of potassium for sodium
      or calcium ions on smectites and interlayered clays. Potassium-based muds perform
     best on shales containing large quantities of smectite or interlayered clays in the total
      clay fraction. Shallow shales, containing large amounts of montmorillonite.
     Potassium interactions with clay surfaces can be traced to two effects: ionic size and
      hydrational energy. Potassium ions are of the proper size to fit snugly into the spaces
     between the two silica tetrahedral layers which contact each other in the formation of a
      three-layer clay packet. The ionic diameter of potassium is 2.66 Å, very close to the
      available distance of 2.8 Å in the lattice space of the clay structure. A cation slightly

      In addition of using KCl, despite Gachsaran is an un-permeable formation and seems

     While drilling this section XC Polymer will be used as base of rheology to extend hole

      In case of necessary the inhibition of system can be increased by adding PHPA which

            Mud Weight
    The starting mud weight  will be 75 pcf Salt Saturated mud, and then   it  will be
     increased gradually to 95 pcf to TD at 1150m. That is valid unless the hole condition
      dictates otherwise. Controlling of MW could be done by running SCE and dressing the
     shakers with finest mesh screens & dumping the sand trap and dilution.

                  Plastic Viscosity
      Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids
      control equipment, coupled with whole new mud dilution.

               Hole Cleaning
     Cleaning cuttings from a vertical hole has been covered extensively by numerous
      investigators. Hole cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the
       slip velocity of the cuttings with sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the
       drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater than the settling velocity of the largest cutting
       will theoretically lift all the cuttings to surface eventually, too low an annular velocity
       will lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in the annulus. Experience
     has shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or
     stuck pipe when circulation is stopped.

               API Fluid Loss Control
         It is recommended that No Control FL down to 500 m, 40-20 cc from 500-1000 m and
       finally around 5 cc from 1000 m to section TD. This may best be achieved by the
      addition of Starch at 12 lb/bbl.

               Rheology
     Maintain the Yield point around 20 lb/100 ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning, making
     adjustment with fresh mud or water as required.

                 Trips
      Prior to tripping,  if any concern exists in regard to hole cleanliness, consideration
     should be given to pumping a high weight  pill while on bottom. This is especially
      important if no pills have been pumped during the section drilled. Returns of all such
       pills at the shakers should be monitored to gauge their effectiveness. Care should be
     exercised to ensure that excessive amounts of high-density pills are not pumped due
      to their effect on hydrostatic head.

      In the case of all pills do not stop or reduce the circulation rate before the pill(s) have
     been evacuated from hole. To do so will result in material dropping out of the pill.
      Circulation should continue if solids are still coming over the shakers.

                 Lithology
         •  Gachsaran Formation
         •  Deposition of the Gachsaran Formation is cyclic. This formation totally consists
              of a repetition of Anhydrite, grey and red marl as well as salt and some
            limestone beds.

               Torque and Drag
      In case of high torque and drag Lubricant would be used at 1-2% volume. Lubricant is

                Corrosion Monitoring
     Corrosion products and corrosion rings should be run throughout this section to monitor
      corrosion rate.

               Rheology & Hydraulics
      Dilution with fresh mud and/or premixes should be made periodically to ensure good
      rheological properties and minimize solids build-up; Rheology should be maintained in
      specification in order to minimize the effects of ECD on the formation.

      Attention should be paid to pump rates and hydraulic models to achieve optimum flow
     regime. Hence avoid washing out borehole sections that may lead to ledges.

                 Solids Control Management
    SCE should be function tested and repaired as necessary prior to spud the well.

     Dress Shakers with 60-80 mesh size screen and mud cleaner with 140-175.

     Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.

    Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear

     motion s h a l e shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at
        all the time at high flow rate on LGS mode (High Speed) to remove low gravity solids
     and keep mud weight & properties in range.

     according to losses. In the event of seepage losses, treat system with a finer grade of
    LCM at 10 – 15 lb/bbl. In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare

              Hydrogen Sulphide
    H2S gas been encountered in offset wells, therefore all necessary precaution should
     be taken in this interval. In case of H2S detection, inhibited water as following formula
     should be prepared and pumped in sequence into the through drill string for 60 bbls
     per each 12 hrs drilling and 60 bbls into the annulus per each 6 hrs.

      Zinc carbonate should be kept 0.7‐1.0 lb/bbl, pH of whole inhibited water mud should
     be increased by Lime or Caustic Soda up to 11.0 then buffer mud system by lime and
     should have 1‐2 lb/bbl excess Lime in system to neutralize H2S gas. To minimize the
       risk of corrosion due to attack of acidic gases, mud system has been formulated by
      corrosion inhibitor at range of 0.5 to 1.0%vol (1.8‐3.5 lb/bbl).
     Corrosion inhibition for the drill string, tubular goods and downhole tools. Corrosion
       inhibition is a water soluble filming amine which forms a protective film on all metal
      surfaces to prevent corrosion attack from oxygen, carbon dioxide and hydrogen
      sulphide.
     While  drilling,  additions  of Corrosion  inhibition should be made according  to
      penetration rate and dilution. Daily treatments should average 0.1 – 0.2% by volume
       for continuous treatment. The recommended concentration to be maintained in the
     system  is dependent upon the corrosive environment. Corrosion rate should be
     monitored with drill pipe corrosion ring.

                   Interval Mud Discussion
      After drilling shoe track and rate hole with carried mud from previous section, treated
     Polymer Mud will be weight up gradually to 105 pcf. 70mt. Before Gachsaran #4 mud
     weight must weighed up to 125 pcf to drilling this hole section. The mud weight could
     be increased to 125±2 pcf if the hole dictates.
     Saturated Salt Muds are primarily used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while
       drilling massive salt beds. They can also be used to reduce dispersion and hydration of
     shale and clay.
      Salt and Salt Saturated Muds are used to prevent excessive hole enlargement while
       drilling massive salt beds. They can also be used to reduce dispersion and hydration of
     shale and clay. Solids content (percent by volume) should be maintained within a
      desired range by mechanical removal or dilution with saturated salt water to prevent
     unacceptable increases in gel strengths and viscosity. The chloride content of saturated
       salt muds is 188,000 mg/l at saturation. As the temperature of the mud increases, more
       salt is able to go into solution. This means that a fluid which is saturated under surface
      conditions may not be saturated in down hole temperatures and can cause substantial
     washout in a salt zone due to increased salt solubility. Control of the pH of saturated
       salt muds varies widely. Saturated salt muds require larger additions of caustic soda to
     maintain a pH  in Salt Saturate Muds. Maintaining an ± 9.5 PH  offers several
     advantages:
       • Deflocculants are more effective
       • Corrosion is reduced
       • Lower concentrations of filtration control additives are required when Ca++ and
    Mg++ solubility is reduced
       • Foaming tendency is lessened
       • Mud is generally more stable
     Saturated salt muds  will normally contain soluble calcium due to the formations
     penetrated and the type of makeup water used. Also, the sodium ions from the salt will
     undergo a base exchange and release calcium ions from the clay platelets, thereby
      contributing to the free calcium. Generally, the presence of calcium does not produce
      detrimental effects on the mud; except when the pH is increased beyond 12.0 and then

                                                                                    Page 113 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
         Mansour Abad Project
   N.I.S.O.C
                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project  Package   Issuer   Facility   Discipline    Doc.    Sequence    Rev.      Page 114 of 208053-073-9125
                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

      the fluid loss will be difficult to control. Foaming is generally restricted to surface foam
     and is not troublesome unless aggravated by mechanical agitation. The degree of
     foaming may sometimes be decreased by increasing the alkalinity of the mud (Pm). A
     De-foaming agent may be necessary. Unless Mg++ sensitive additives are used, a
     Saturated Salt Mud is less prone to foam and air cut with a 9.5 - 10 PH. The temperature
       limitation of Saturated Salt Muds is around 250°F and is normally dictated by the
       filtration control additive used. Ca++ and Mg++ hardness does not adversely affect
       filtration control in Saturated Salt Muds when using starch; however, usually there are
     no problems associated with saturated salt mud conversions. Conversion can be
     accomplished in two circulations. The mixing hopper discharge should be located away
     from the main pump suctions to reduce foaming and air cutting. When a freshwater mud
       is to be converted to a saturated salt mud, it is desirable to use as much of the old mud
     as possible. The amount of salt required to saturate the system should be calculated
     and then added through the hopper. A saturated salt mud will generally weight 75 pcf
      without weight material addition. Next, a fluid loss additive is added through the hopper
      while the mud is circulated. Starch is generally used for fluid loss control and as a
     supplementary viscosifier. Normally, 9 - 12 lb/bbl starch will be required to obtain a fluid
      loss of less than 3 cc/30 minutes. If a higher density is required, Barite which will be
     use. When weighting up with Barite, a Lignosulphonate Deflocculant is recommended
      to avoid excessive viscosity and high gel strengths as contingency.
    Due to probability of hydrocarbon gas because of geological maps, which is Located
     between two thrust faults, of Khaviz structures, Keep contingency stock of Lime and
     Zinc Source chemicals on location.

                Mixing Procedure
    Mud Type: Salt Saturated Polymer Mud

      1.   Fill the cleaned tanks with the required volume of drill water
      2.  Treat out any hardness greater than 700ppm with soda ash 1-3 ppb.
      3.  Weight up with salt up to 74.5 pcf (Salt Saturated)
      4. Add 9-12 ppb starch to salt water and then mix 10 to 15 minutes in reserve tank to
         increase Fluid loss control (7-9 ppb starch should be added to mud to fluid loss
          control)
      5. Use 1 - 2 ppb PAC-L and mix it for at least 5 minutes.
      6.  Weight up with Barite to 125 pcf adjusted with the whole condition
      7. Add 0.5-2 ppb Lime or caustic soda to control PH
      8.  Add 1-3 ppb Xanthan Gum (as needed).

      Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids
      control equipment, coupled with whole new mud dilution.

               Hole Cleaning
     Cleaning cuttings from a vertical hole has been covered extensively by numerous
      investigators. Hole cleaning in a vertical hole is essentially a matter of overcoming the
       slip velocity of the cuttings with sufficient annular velocity and carrying capacity of the
       drilling fluid. Although any velocity greater than the settling velocity of the largest cutting
       will theoretically lift all the cuttings to surface eventually, too low an annular velocity will
     lead to an undesirable high concentration of cuttings in the annulus. Experience has
    shown that cuttings concentrations more than 5% by volume cause tight hole or stuck
     pipe when circulation is stopped.

               API Fluid Loss Control
         It is recommended that FL < 3 cc from 1600 to section TD. This may best be achieved
     by the addition of Starch at 12 lb/bbl and PAC LV at 1-3 lb/bbl.
     Note: The mud weight could be increased to 125±2 pcf if the hole dictates, If Mud weight
      of system increase more than 125 PCF using STARCH HT as fluid loss controller and
     keeping FL< 2 cc.

               Rheology
     Maintain the Yield point around 20 lb/100 ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning, making
     adjustment with fresh mud or water as required.

                  Total Hardness
      Total  hardness  should be  maintained  below 800 mg/L  for optimum  polymer
     performance with the addition of Soda Ash.

                 Trips

     be given to pumping a high weight pill while on bottom. This is especially important if no

                Corrosion monitoring
     Corrosion products and corrosion rings should be run throughout this section to monitor

               Rheology & Hydraulics
      Dilution with fresh mud and/or premixes should be made periodically to ensure good
      rheological properties and minimize solids build-up; Rheology should be maintained in
      specification in order to minimize the effects of ECD on the formation.
      Attention should be paid to pump rates and hydraulic models to achieve optimum flow
     regime. Hence avoid washing out hole sections that may lead to ledges.

                 Solids Control Management
     Dress Shakers with 140 - 175 mesh size screen and mud cleaner with 230 mesh.
     Ensure shakers are running immediately prior to and during all periods of circulation.
    Use all the solids control equipment available on the rig site. The combination of linear
     motion shale shaker with centrifuge proved best results. Centrifuge should be run at all
      the time at high flow rate on barite recovery mode to remove low gravity solids and keep
    mud weight & properties in range.
     Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment.
       All efforts should be made to maintain the LGS below 7%.

            Down Hole Losses
     Losses are expected while drilling this section. The concentration of LCM will vary
     according to losses. In the event of seepage losses, treat system with a finer grade of
    LCM at 10 – 15 lb/bbl. In the event of moderate to high rate of well bore loss, prepare
       pills at different graded concentrations and spot over thief zone. The concentration may
     vary between 20 – 70 lb/bbl. Ensure that the driller displace the LCM pill out of the string
      prior to shutting down the mud pumps. In the event of severe losses, cross linking pills
     should be pumped to minimize losses.

       Mud Discussion

    The 8-1/2” hole section will be drilled through the Asmari to 2834m EM/ OBM would be
     used to clean this section and run 7” liner. EM/OBM for this interval has been formulated
     base on 55.5-63 pcf. This type of mud is a highly inhibitive system and will provide a
     very stable, in gauge, wellbore under normal circumstances. This system provides the
     best insurance for ensuring a trouble-free operation in an inclined wellbore, including
     reduced torque and drag, no bit balling as well as improved ROP’s.
         It should be noted that due to EM/OBM’s providing an “in gauge” hole, attention should
     be paid to drag when pulling pipe either on connections or tripping. It can be very easy
      to become stuck by pulling into a gauge hole with a small number of cuttings around
      the BHA; this will increase the possibility of incoming
     mechanically stuck. At the first sign of excessive drag (> 20 klb.), slack of the drill string
     and either pump or rotate the pipe to clear the obstruction before continuing to pull the
       string. This is particularly important in the first 5 stands when tripping out of the hole.
     Whereas Asmari reservoirs  is mainly composed of limestone and dolomite. This
     limestone is light gray, tan, Archie type I A interbedded with type I /II and II, Wackstone
      to Packstone by Dunham. The dolomite is sandy, Anhydritic and sometimes highly
     porous and fractured crystalline carbonate. Microfossils in the carbonates included:
      Borelismelocurdica, Miogypsinoides, complantus, Elphidum sp. When TD is reached, a
    minimum of two circulations should be pumped prior to make a wiper trip to surface,
      followed by a circulation when back on bottom prior to pull out of the hole.

          4. Add 0.5-1 ppb Viscosifier (As needed)

            HTHP Fluid Loss Control
    The Fluid loss for Emulsion mud is NC during drilling Asmari formation. The HTHP for
   OBM will be maintained at or below 4 ml/30 minute (250 °F / 500 psi) with no water
     present in the filtrate in OBM.  It is important that the filtrate be water free to avoid water-
      wetting of the formation and cuttings. A rising trend in filtrate quantity will indicate a
     need for more emulsifiers, and the results of this test are a better indication of emulsion
       stability than the emulsion stability meter.

               Rheology
      Particular attention should be paid to increasing rheology brought about through
      incorporation of drilled solids into the active system. Control is best achieved by whole
    mud dilution and effective solids removal. Excessive viscosity can be detrimental to
      solids control efficiency leading to expensive treatment.
    The 3 rpm will be maintained at or above a minimum of 7 This will be sufficient to
      optimize hole cleaning. The 6rpm reading should be obtained with properly sheared.
     Gels will be minimal at this low mud weight, 30-minute gel must be checked and
      reported to ensure that the gel profile is flat and non-progressive.

                   Alkalinity
     Emulsion mud PH should be kept around 7-8 to prevent any two phases.
      Oil base mud, the alkalinity should be maintained in the range of 4 - 5 ppb excess lime.
     Depletion and/or acid gasses may necessitate regular additions of lime to maintain this
       level. The alkalinity can be maintained at similar levels to that seen on conventional
      invert emulsion systems. Oil based mud is tolerant to Calcium contamination.

           Drilling Issues

               Stuck Pipe
     Pipe Lax pill at 3 - 5 gal / bbl of Diesel can be spotted around the stuck area. For more
      information, refer to Stuck Pipe Appendix.

               Hole Cleaning
    The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning is the 6 and 3 readings. The 6
     reading has to be over 7 all time to ensure good hole cleaning. Sweep hole at regular
      intervals with viscous pills.
      1. Forget the Bottoms Up calculations based on hole geometry and pump rate. It will
     take at least 100% excess circulating to get bottoms up; probably more.
      2. Pump as fast as possible. This may require running larger jets, larger liners, and
     minimizing pressure losses inside the drill string.
      3. Spinning drill pipes. Larger drill pipe allows higher AV's by minimizing pressure losses

                                                                                    Page 128 of 208

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
         Mansour Abad Project
   N.I.S.O.C
                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project  Package   Issuer   Facility   Discipline    Doc.    Sequence    Rev.      Page 129 of 208053-073-9125
                  MB     W061N    PEDCO     110        DR      DM         0112        02

      inside the drill string and by providing a smaller annular area. In some areas 6 5/8" drill
     pipe is used. Most derricks that can hold 5" DP can also accommodate 5 1/2".
      4. The reciprocation & rotation of the drill string, along with proper rheology, will normally
     improve hole cleaning. Also,  it seems that rotation of the drill string more effectively
     removes cuttings in a viscous mud vs. a mud where viscosity & gels are insufficient.
      5. You might consider the relationship between the pump flow rate & BHA pulling speed
    when making a wiper trip. Relatively slow pulling speeds and high pump rates will
     normally assist in enhancing hole cleaning. Also, any cuttings bed remaining when
      pulling at higher speeds is thicker than the bed left when pulling at a slower speed, for
      the same pump flow rate.
      6. Control ROP's (including instantaneous ROP). 100 ft/hr in a 12 ¼" hole produces a
    minimum of 15 bbls of cutting that has to be removed from the hole.
      7. In laminar flow the hole cleaning capacity, especially at low shear rates in large
     diameter sections, can be improved by raising the low shear-rate viscosity & gels. The
     best indicators will be the 6 & 3 rpm and initial gel. A rule of thumb is to have the low
      shear-rate values approximately the same as the hole size.
      8. Another data  points  to consider measuring  is the  relaxing  time. Relaxation
     measurements are made  after the standard viscosity determinations have been
     compiled with the viscometer. After you have determined the last viscosity (3 rpm), shut
      the viscometer off and measure the time it takes for the dial to fall back to zero. Fluids
     which  exhibit an extended relaxation time  indicate improved hole cleaning and
     suspension characteristics.

              Hydrogen Sulphide
    The mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of H2S, if smell of H2S is been
      detected, treat the mud with 1.0 - 2.0 ppb H2S Scavenger.

            LCM Pill Spotting Procedure

         •   After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30
            minutes and monitor the annulus.
         •   After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full.  If the hole can be
                  filled, close the BOP and squeeze 10 bbls of LCM pill into the formation without
            exceeding 200 psi.
         •    If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
         •  Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then
           mix
           and spot another 50 bbls of LCM pill.
         •  Attempt to fill the annulus.  If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbls of
        LCM pill into the formation without exceeding 200 psi.   If a squeeze pressure
            develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before staging the drill string back to
            bottom.

             Recommended procedure to reduce surface losses
     Every effort should be made to eliminate surface losses of OBM mud. Mud maintenance
      costs are normally attributed to volume building from new hole drilled and surface
      losses. Normal surface losses can be held to a minimum using the following techniques.
         •  Used a mud saver sub. The use of this will reduce losses on connections.
         •  Use pipe wipers to remove oil mud from the drill pipe on trips.
         •   Install a catch pan on the top of the bell nipple. This must be large enough to
            extend  beyond  the  edges   of  the   rotary   table.  This  device   will
            catch mud which  falls through the table and  will divert  it into the  drilling
              nipple.
         •  A racking pan should be provided for the drill pipe. A return line from this pan
           must be run to the flow line or into the catch pan described in the above item.
         •  A mud box should be used on trips. A mud box in good condition will prevent
             serious losses when pulling a wet string. The mud box should be connected to
             the flow line or catch pan.
         •  Keep water hoses off of the rig floor and away from mud tanks. Water additions
              to  oil mud should be made only upon the recommendations of the mud

        Completion Fluid Discussion

          Type A: Diesel treated with H2S, Corrosion inhibitor Fluid Systems
     •  Mixing Procedure:

    Completion fluid Mixing Procedure (Diesel inhibition):

      1. Fill up tank as require Diesel.
      2. Added 0.2-0.5% V/ V: H2S, Corrosion inhibitor (completion type).

          Type B: Solids-Free NaCl Fluid Systems
     This fluid is recommended to make from fresh water or is solutions made with water
     and the addition of one or more electrolytes. These fluids do not contain either
     suspended particles or viscosifier, which mean neither filtration control nor viscosity
      control, are provided. Some NaCl  is corrosive and when corrosion inhibitors are
      required,  compatibility  studies  should be  performed. Some  brine  is  toxic and
     precautions should be taken to prevent contact with unprotected skin. Brine solutions
     can be prepared to give good inhibition of clays or shales in producing formations. In
      addition, common contaminants do not affect the brines.

      Salt solutions were formerly considered too corrosive to be used as work-over or
     completion fluids or as acker fluids. The corrosion problem can be solved by adjusting
      the pH of the solution to above 10.5 - 11; however, PH measurements may be less
      important than measuring and controlling the PH-alkalinity of the filtrate; this value
     should be kept above 1 cc. Caustic Soda will be used for pH control.

     Adjustment of PH, or alkalinity, does not necessarily ensure the solution to be corrosion
      resistant. It may be necessary to use a corrosion inhibitor to achieve lower corrosion
      rates.

     •  Mixing Procedure:

    Completion fluid Mixing Procedure (Fresh water inhibition):

         Engineering Comment

           Corrosion Control
     Corrosion control  in completion  fluids  is important to protect tubular goods and
     equipment. Corrosion can be limited by controlling the fluid PH at the neutral or alkaline
       level, and  treating out dissolved oxygen.  In severe environments such as high
     temperature or contamination with acid gases, the addition of filming amines can limit
      corrosion to acceptable levels.

    The completion fluid for this well will be Diesel or Local water treated with an inhibitor.

       Pit management will be a key in the successful completion of this interval and sufficient
     time for planning and preparation should be allowed.

       All valves should be checked for leakage beforehand and defects identified to be
      reported and rectified by drilling contractor.

    The rig pumps are to displace all clean up pills. Prepare spacers and wash pills as per
     program in the tanks. Ensure that sufficient spacer is prepared to account for any dead
     tanks volume.

     Prepare all inhibited Diesel or NACL before starting the displacement process. After
     preparing the brine should be filtered through filtration unit and store in a clean pit before
     displacement.

              Filtration Process
       Filtration provides clean fluids that will prevent damage to the formation, the reservoir
     and its permeability. It does this by removal of solids and particulates from the fluid that
    may otherwise block the open space  within the rock formation containing the
     hydrocarbon fluid within the production zone.

    Any solids and contaminates in the completion fluid will reduce its effectiveness. An
       efficiently filtered and completely solid free completion fluid will add value to both the
      productivity and the dependability of the well in the long term.

     dual pod filtration cartridge unit or Filter Press is recommended for filtering brines and
     produced water in completion, stimulation, and work over operations. The pods are
     connected by a manifold, providing staged filtration capability. Staged filtration utilizes
      cartridge filters with different ratings to maximize filtration efficiency. Cartridge filtration
       is designed for use with fluids containing a low percent by volume of suspended solids.
      Cartridge filtration is not economic when fluids are contaminated with  oil or other
     substances.

           Rig Clean Up Check List
     •  Areas to clean:

      1. Surface pits.

      2. Clean the suction, return, settling, and reserve pits.

      3. Clean the sand traps.

      6. Clean the shaker area including all solids equipment and lines.

      7. Clean the mixing hoppers.

      8. Clean the cement unit.

      9. Clean any other pits or equipment that the completion fluid may contact.

      11. Waste Management Program

       NOTE: Final DWM program will be issue by service company in due time.

        Base on waste pit profile facility at Rig site for allocating waste management equipment,
              all wastes include dump drilling/completion fluids (Including WBM, OBM, Emulsion Mud,
         Cement, Acid, etc.) and surface waters will be conducted and collected in the waste pit
          during the operation. Dewatering package has been considered to recover the waste
          water for re-use in washing, cementing and drilling operations. At the end of drilling
          operation and after rig moving and total evaporation of remained waste water, the dried
           cutting will be transported to assigned location by Company as disposal area.
          Following is a calculation table of produced cuttings and estimated total mud dump
         volume for this well.

   12. Health, Safety and Environment
        General Quality, Health, Safety & Environmental
      Requirements
      Rig & Rig-Less Drilling and Completion operations HSE goals are:
          1. Zero harmful chemical spill
          2. Zero incidents (Human, environment, asset and reputation)
          3. Zero serious well control situations
          4. No flaring for minimum emission to air
          5. Rig prepared for H2S
          6. High standard on housekeeping
          7. Hands on Safety focus
          8. Water consumption shall be minimized
          9. Comply with  all applicable  oil & gas industry rules, standards and
             regulations.

      For this well, the special HSE focus points & HSE program to be followed will be:

         1.  Fire protection, Firefighting and no explosive chance
         2.  Lifting Operation, falling objects, fall from height
         3. Job Safety Analysis (JSA) shall be used for planning of all non-standard
            or unfamiliar operations.
         4. Good communication is the key to good teamwork. Radio communication
           should be used between crew members to improve communication.
         5. Use of proper PPE relates to the employee’s jobs.
         6. Pre-job meetings shall be held prior to all special jobs such as Radioactive
           Logging, Acidizing, DST, Cementing, Casing running, etc.
         7. PTW System Shall be run and all special activity and jobs started after
            raised permit to work.

────────────────────────────────────────────

         8. Rig & service provider crew shall be trained & prepared for H2S Release.
           Regular drills shall be held.
         9. Derrick shall be inspecting regularly for loose objects or potential dropped
            objects.  In  addition,  inspections  should be performed  after  sever
             vibrations/jarring operations.
        10. All  critical equipment such as BOP system, hoisting system,  driller
           equipment, etc. should be periodically inspecting by HSE Check list.
        11. Pre spud checklist should be completed before starting any activity.
        12. Pre-Spud check list must be verified by PEDCO before operation.

        13. All incidents and non-conformances shall be reported to PEDCO HSE
          Department by the Drilling supervisor.
        14. At all-time required minimum amount of Salt and Barite shall to be on
          board to increase mud weight around 1.0 PPG (Min. requirement ≈ +/-
          100 MT).
        15. Enough Cement shall be available to prepare 400 m of cement plugs.
        16. Flow meter will be used to measure the flow rate.
        17. An H2S service company will be assigned to control the risk of H2S.
         More information is detailed on H2S Monitoring and Control chapter.
           Tables below will identify the list of equipment used in this regard.
           Meanwhile, information regarding the concentration of the gas appears
              in engineering documents.
        18. Sewage treatment package shall be provided by rig contractor (NIDC
            or …), as per the contract.
        19. As per the contractor HSE Plan, all HSE statistical reports, incident
            reports & statistics of other HSE activities will be included in daily &
           monthly HSE reports of the drilling rig contractor.
        20. Waste Management Program will be followed as described in Waste
         Management Program chapter.

       Meetings
   HSE meetings shall be convened on a monthly basis with an agenda to
     discuss the general issues about HSE, any change in the contractor, in the
     nature and risk of the activities, HSE training program, safety analysis of the
      activities, as well as investigation and analysis of the accidents. The
     Contractor’s site manager and HSE Representative shall attend such meetings
    and report to the Client’s site manager and HSE representative.
    Weekly HSE meeting shall be conducted with the presence of PEDCO HSE &
     Rig Contractor HSE Supervisor.

        Well Control
         1.  All well control equipment such as BOP Stack, Chock manifold and
           Accumulator unit shall be certified by competent third party and keep all
              certificate onboard.
         2. BOP test shall be done after every nipple up and any maintenance on
        BOP also shall be done in accordance to routine well program and
         company policy.
         3. The BOP shall not be removed until the well has been properly plugged
            or secured.
         4. Accumulator shall be equipped with secondary power supply.
         5. The following well control materials shall be maintained on the rig at all
            times:
         Sufficient weight control material to increase the weight of the active
           mud system by 1 ppg or the amount stipulated on the approved drilling
                permit, whichever is greater.
         Sufficient cement to allow a 400-foot plug to be set.
         6. The Person In charge (PIC) shall suspend drilling operations any time
           these materials are not available, and shall not resume drilling until they
          have been delivered to the facility.
         7.  Trip drill, Pit drill, BOP drill, Choke drill and other drills shall be carried out
           weekly as conditions permit and at the discretion of the PIC and the
           Operator’s Representative. All drills will be performed in accordance with
            the procedures in this manual and the PIC will record them on the drill
             report.
            Specific drills to be carried out include:
         Kick while tripping
         Kick while drilling
          Instructions to divert
              Other drills may include:

────────────────────────────────────────────

       H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure
     As per NISOC SOW Mansour Abad Asmari reservoir contain H2S, so precautions shall
     be taken in place especially in 8-1/2” hole section (Asmari Reservoir) while drilling,
      completion and well testing operation.
     H2S can be released any time while drilling, completion and well testing operation,
       therefore:
      The Rig shall be prepared for H2S (Training, procedures and protective
            gear).
      Make sure everyone on the Rig should be made aware of the hazard
           presented by H2S during their induction when they first arrive on the rig.
      The mud shall be treated to protect the drill pipe and the casing.
       All training program shall be recorded and reported.

    13. H2S Monitoring & Control

     Due to lack of data from NISOC and uncertainty regarding to Khaviz cap rock structure
      and fluid beneath cap rock, it is highly recommended to consider safety requirements
       while  drilling through this hole section such as use Gas/H2S requirements (H2S
       Service, Gas Tight and H2S inhibitor additive for mud and CMT) must be consider
       before drilling 17-1/2” Hole section and As per NISOC SOW, the Asmari reservoir in
      Mansour Abad oilfield contain H2S for this reason, it is planned to use H2S service in 8-
       1/2” Hole section and following requirements would be noted:
